correctness.rationale: For \(\varphi_c(z)=1+z+cz^2\), the Schwarz factorization \(\omega=zv\) gives the exact derivative identity \(S_f=(1+2czv)v' +(c-1/2)v^2-czv^3-c^2z^2v^4/2\). Schwarz--Pick and the triangle inequality give the explicit majorants \(F_+\) and \(F_-\). On \(0\le c\le1/2\), convexity in \(c\) and nonnegative endpoint decompositions prove the upper bound one. For \(c=-d\), an exact polynomial sum of squares is nonnegative exactly up to \(d=(\sqrt3-1)/2\). Its strict gap away from \(z=0,v=0\) forces every norm extremizer to have \(v(z)=e^{i\theta}z\), which integrates to the stated complete family. For larger \(d\le1/2\), a real disk automorphism aligns all Schwarzian phases and yields \(F_-(d,ds,s)=1+(d^2+d-1/2)s^2+O(s^4)>1\). The supporting symbolic checker was executed from its actual path. Ahlfors--Weill with hyperbolic norm at most one gives the stated at-most-three quasiconformal extension.

originality.rationale: The original 2026 Allu--Kumar article computes Hankel determinants on a positive quadratic-target family and does not address Schwarzian norms or signed parameters. Kanas--Sugawa (2011), the decisive broad comparison, provides a general sharp variational expression for Schwarzian norms for analytic target functions, but the inspected theorem and its proof do not evaluate this signed quadratic target, determine the exact radical transition, or classify all extremizers. The positive/negative phase decomposition and matching automorphism obstruction give a new explicit result requiring additional parameter optimization. Nearby Janowski-convex and pre-Schwarzian studies address distinct functions or invariants. Searches of published records for aliases, the exact polynomial target and the radical boundary did not locate an evaluated equivalent theorem. Residual risk: an unindexed exact computation, or treatment of this specialization as immediately covered by the general 2011 variational formula.
residual_risks: The 2011 general sharp variational formula already encodes the target norm as an implicit optimization; a different evaluation of its quadratic special case may exist under an unexpected title or be considered an elementary corollary.
Full texts of the nearby Janowski norm and pre-Schwarzian articles were not inspected, although their documented target/invariant scopes differ from this theorem.
The result gives a sharp *Schwarzian* cutoff, not an optimal quasiconformal extension dilatation threshold.

value.rationale: The parameter interval \(|c|\le1/2\) is precisely the natural real univalence range of the quadratic target. The recent source studied its positive half, while the signed continuation probes how much of the class remains under global Schwarzian and quasiconformal control when target positivity fails. The exact radical threshold is a structural phase transition in a natural global invariant, with a matched nontrivial automorphism obstruction and a complete equality classification. It yields a non-obvious uniform quasiconformal extension guarantee for negative-parameter classes that are not assumed convex. This motivation does not depend on a numerical cutoff, a mere normalization check, or a routine fixed-parameter coefficient calculation.
